text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementAstronomyNASA Shares Image of a Galactic Smiley FaceJCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleNature has blessed us with brains that are hardwired to find patterns and recognize faces, so it’s no surprise we tend to notice faces even where there aren’t any. Although they may be better educated, the humans at NASA are no different than the rest of us. They recently posted an image of a smiley face discovered amongst the stars. Powered By 10 ShareNextStayThe galaxy cluster SDSS J1038+4849 as imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope. Credit: NASA/ESAThe photo, originally captured by the Hubble Space Telescope in 2015, shows a galaxy cluster known as SDSS J1038+4849 located 4.5 billion light-years from Earth in the Big Dipper constellation. In the photo, the two yellow “eyes” are actually massive galaxies.
